newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end mixed on end-account selling.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed on end-account selling.

text.p: End-of-account profit-taking pulled shares to a mixed close across Indian exchanges on Friday after prices rallied in early trade, brokers said.
The Bombay share index finished up 15.84 points, or 0.42 percent, at 3,769.34, off 3,812.82 intra-day high.
Focus remained on bank stocks that have caught market fancy buoyed by hopes of economic revival, they said.
"We saw profit-taking in these (bank) stocks," said Kuntal Shah, chief dealer at broker D.T. Gandhi. "The market ended flat, but the outlook remains positive."

India's lower house of parliament on Friday approved the 1997/98 (April-March) Finance Bill, the cornerstone of the centre-left government's market-friendly budget proposals that slashed taxes and tariffs.
Traders said the passage of the budget, presented on February 28 and held hostage by a political crisis, would infuse confidence among foreign investors.
"The market can look forward to focus on positive factors such as monsoon forecasts, as the budget uncertainty is finally over," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Expectations of an increase in government-controlled oil prices will overshadow trading next week, but traders see shares staying higher.
Fresh demand could come from foreign funds which see blue-chip stocks as buy opportunities, brokers said.
India imports most of its oil but sells to domestic consumers at lower than world prices. Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral recently said he intended to raise oil prices.
